title: Moses on Nebo (Deuteronomy 34)
hook: he sees the promised land and dies before entering

segments.voice: Yesterday, choose life: two roads laid out plainly, and Moses pleading for one. Your line was the word is very near you. Which fork did you take? Day three hundred eighty-nine.

An old man climbs a mountain alone. Behind him, in the plains of Moab, a whole people is camped and waiting. He has walked with them through a sea, a desert, a golden calf, a long run of complaints and a long run of mercies. At the top of Nebo, God shows him everything: the hills of the north, the far sea in the west, the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees. Every place he spent his life walking toward. And then God tells him plainly: you have seen it with your eyes. You will not go over. The last chapter of Deuteronomy begins here.
screen: `AN OLD MAN CLIMBS NEBO.` → `THE WHOLE LAND IN VIEW.` → `YOU WILL NOT GO OVER.`

segments.voice: First, why. Back in the book of Numbers, at a place called Meribah, the people were dying of thirst, and God told Moses to speak to a rock. Moses, angry, struck it twice instead. Water came. But God told him then: you won't bring this people into the land. Readers still argue about why that moment counted so much. The text doesn't fully explain it. Second, the death. Moses climbs Nebo, God shows him the whole land, and then, the text says, Moses the servant of the Lord died there, according to the word of the Lord. In Hebrew, literally, at the mouth of the Lord; Jewish tradition came to say God took his soul with a kiss. He was a hundred and twenty, and his eye was not dim. God himself buries him, and no one knows his grave to this day. No shrine, no pilgrimage site. Third, the people and the next leader. They weep for him thirty days. Joshua, full of the spirit of wisdom, takes over. And the book closes: there never arose again a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. Fourth, how the story goes on. One opinion in the Talmud says Joshua wrote these last verses, since Moses couldn't describe his own burial. And the Gospels bring Moses back once more, on a mountain inside the land, talking with Jesus at the Transfiguration; Luke says they spoke of the exodus Jesus would accomplish in Jerusalem. The night before he was killed in 1968, Martin Luther King Junior told a church in Memphis he had been to the mountaintop and seen the promised land, and might not get there with them.
screen: `STRIKING THE ROCK AT MERIBAH.` · `HE DIES AT THE MOUTH OF THE LORD.` · `NO ONE KNOWS HIS GRAVE.` · `NO PROPHET LIKE MOSES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with a hope you won't see finished. Settle, and breathe. Think of something you're working toward that is bigger than your lifetime. A child or grandchild growing up. A parish that will outlast you. A cause, a garden, a cure, a family healing that may take generations. Picture the far end of it, the land across the river. Let yourself want it. And let yourself accept, gently, that you may only see it from the mountain. That doesn't make your part smaller. If you pray, you can entrust it to God, who buried Moses himself. If you don't, just hold it with open hands. The bell holds the time.
Nebo. The mountain where the prophet the Lord knew face to face was shown the whole promised land, and died before he could enter it. Today's word.
Your line: some only see it. Today, put one stone into something you won't see finished, and let that be enough. Day three hundred eighty-nine.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Moses as a holy prophet, and pilgrims visit Mount Nebo in Jordan, where a Franciscan-cared-for church and lookout stand over the Jordan valley, though the text says no one knows where Moses is buried.

fork.setup: you're Moses, a hundred and twenty years old, on top of Nebo. God shows you the whole land you've walked toward for forty years. what happens next?
options: you cross the Jordan and lead them in.
you die there, and God buries you where no one knows.
fork.reveal: he dies on Nebo at the word of the Lord, and God himself buries him. the people weep thirty days, and Joshua leads them on.

original.note: Hebrew: Nebo, the mountain in Moab facing Jericho across the Jordan, where Moses saw the land and died.

trapdoor: what you thought: a sad ending where Moses gets punished.
what it means: a life given to a journey whose end he only saw, buried by God, with no prophet like him after.
what a scholar hears: he died al-pi YHWH, at the mouth of the Lord; rabbis said by a kiss, and the Talmud says Joshua wrote the last eight verses.

sources.ref: Martin Luther King Jr., 'I've Been to the Mountaintop' (Memphis, April 3, 1968)
